hero.heading: Hanami Festival.
hero.deck: A spring gathering for the MIT community with food, tea, games, calligraphy, origami, and Japanese culture booths.

report.heading: Rainy weekend, full room.
report.note: Hanami Festival 2026 is now closed. Even with weekend rain, the event drew about 350 participants. Sushi sold out in the first 30 minutes, and the shogi, origami, calligraphy, kendama, and other booths stayed lively throughout the evening.

overview.heading: Cherry-blossom season, indoors at MIT scale.
overview.note: Hanami is JAM's broadest cultural welcome: easy to enter, volunteer-powered, and built around food, conversation, and hands-on booths.

programs.title: Food
programs.body: Free sushi and Japanese refreshments create the first reason to gather, then the tables turn into conversation spaces.

programs.title: Culture booths
programs.body: Matcha, shogi, origami, calligraphy, and other booths give visitors a way to participate instead of only watch.

programs.title: Volunteers
programs.body: JAM members organize registration, serving, booths, crowd flow, and cleanup so the event can stay warm and accessible.

hero.deck: Understanding Japan through science, risk, and resilience.

overview.heading: A clear evening on natural risk and how societies prepare.
overview.note: The event combines a short tsunami video, expert talks, Q&A, and audience conversation. Complimentary sushi boxes and O-i Ocha will be available during networking after the talks.

programs.title: Science
programs.body: Why earthquakes and tsunamis happen around Japan, and how scientists read the forces beneath the surface.

programs.title: Infrastructure
programs.body: How transportation, built systems, and disaster planning respond to recurring natural risk.

programs.title: Resilience
programs.body: How communities prepare, recover, and preserve knowledge across generations.

mealBand.heading: Free sushi box + O-i Ocha.
paragraphs: After the talks, registered attendees can enjoy a complimentary sushi box and O-i Ocha during the networking reception.
mealBand.alt: Sushi box served with O-i Ocha

items.label: MIT EAPS
items.name: Ayako Tsuchiyama
items.body: MIT Earth, Atmospheric and Planetary Sciences PhD.

items.label: Infrastructure
items.name: Kota Konishi
items.body: Assistant manager, Central Japan Railway Company; MIT System Design and Management.
items.bio: Kota has spent about six years at Central Japan Railway Company (JR Central), working on Shinkansen rolling stock maintenance and the implementation and management of rolling stock inspection facilities. He has also joined a project supporting the introduction of new rolling stock for Taiwan High Speed Rail. He is currently pursuing a master's degree in MIT System Design and Management (SDM), where he studies the design and management of complex socio-technical systems. After graduation, he plans to work on systems design for Shinkansen rolling stock.

items.label: Seismology
items.name: Yo Kanno
items.body: Japan Meteorological Agency, Seismology and Volcanology Department.

items.label: Disaster management
items.name: Kenji Takahashi
items.body: Former Director-General for Disaster Management, Cabinet Office; former MLIT Deputy Vice-Minister for Policy Coordination.

supportNote.heading: Event support.
supportNote.note: Beneath the Great Wave is supported by the Consulate-General of Japan in Boston. JAM also welcomes future partners for lecture and cultural programming.
